items.title: Children in state care being lured into 'trap houses'
items.description: The ABC has spoken with experts, advocates and residential care workers as part of a 19-month investigation into the sexual exploitation of children in state care.

items.title: Ex-ASIO source denied visa to give evidence at Bondi royal commission
items.description: The man who previously warned ASIO about the Bondi gunmen will not be able to give sensitive and classified evidence at the Royal Commission into Antisemitism and Social Cohesion.

items.title: Thousands of Australians get their news from this site. Its editor doesn't exist
items.description: A "right of centre" website claiming to be news, with more than 42,000 Facebook followers, may not be as independent as it says. An ABC NEWS Verify investigation has found the site uses AI and a fake news editor.

items.title: Live: PM announces Fair Work Court, defends tax changes at ALP national conference
items.description: Speaking at the ALP national conference, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese says the federal government will create a Fair Work Court. Follow live.

items.title: Live: Unemployment rate remains steady
items.description: The Australian share market has opened in the green after Tesla shares tumbled on cash flow news. The unemployment rate has remains steady. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: OpenAI model goes rogue during testing and hacks startup
items.description: OpenAI has announced one of its AI models broke containment during testing before hacking into another AI startup.

items.title: Mamdani says he cannot arrest Netanyahu in New York but US government can
items.description: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani concedes he cannot order the arrest of Benjamin Netanyahu and calls on the US government to take action, but a former international prosecutor warns it could be complicated.

items.title: 'Nervous' investors retreat from housing market as downturn broadens
items.description: Australia's property market has entered a downturn after both house and unit prices fell for the first time in more than three years, bringing an end to the recent housing boom.

items.title: From Mumbai to New York, young Indians gather in unprecedented movement
items.description: A student who started a youth uprising across India is fast becoming the biggest challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's 12-year reign.

items.title: Tongan women 'auctioned off' for marriage in China
items.description: The ABC has spoken to multiple Tongan women who have been lured into an arranged marriage syndicate operating in China, with allegations of passports being confiscated and tens of thousands of dollars changing hands.

items.title: Serious corruption findings against senior ACT public servants
items.description: The commission investigated whether officials were impartial and honest in awarding an $18.8 million refurbishment contract at Campbell Primary School to Lendlease, despite a bid by local firm Manteena being deemed better and cheaper.

items.title: Record $60k fine for man behind 'brazen' dump site that will cost $1m to clean
items.description: The owner of one of Victoria's worst illegal dump sites has been handed a record fine of $60,000 and ordered to pay an expected $1 million to clean up the polluted property in Melbourne's outer north-east.

items.title: The 'fairy gold dust passport' more Australians are chasing
items.description: Australians are racing to secure Irish citizenship, with new figures showing applications have more than doubled in the past three years as people seek the right to live, work and study across the EU.

items.title: Aussie captain relishes 'special' chance 'to take time to be a dad'
items.description: As Nathan Power looks to lead the Australian Sharks at the World Aquatics Water Polo World Cup Finals in Sydney this week, the 33-year-old reflects on how fatherhood has changed his outlook, and how valuable his six-month paternity leave is.

items.title: Many of us want to read more. Here's how to do that
items.description: More than half of us want to read more. Here's how to find your gateway genre and make that happen.

items.title: The intriguing film that casts the 'superior' Jude Law as the insidious Putin
items.description: Cannes darling Oliver Assayas tackles the shadowy forces of our time in his latest film, The Wizard of the Kremlin.

items.title: Nintendo raised prices due to US tariffs. Now, it doesn't want to pass on refunds
items.description: Nintendo has argued it has no duty to pass its refunds onto US consumers. It's the latest in a lengthy tariff fight.

items.title: Prince George turns 13 as he heads to Eton
items.description: Prince George, second in line to the throne, has turned 13 as he readies to follow in his father Prince William's footsteps and start at the prestigious Eton College.

items.title: Rebel Wilson's victory in defamation case could be short-lived. Here's why
items.description: As lawyers for actor Charlotte MacInnes plan to appeal a failed defamation case outcome against Hollywood star Rebel Wilson, a solicitor says the judge's interpretations could be grounds for a retrial or a different verdict.

items.title: US and Saudi Arabia reach nuclear power deal
items.description: Israeli officials and US politicians from both parties have voiced concern that a civilian nuclear project in Saudi Arabia could be used to eventually develop nuclear weapons.

items.title: Trump threatens Iranian power plants, bridges if ships attacked in Hormuz
items.description: US strikes have already widened from the south to western and central areas of Iran in recent days.

items.title: At the CPAC London conference, someone fell asleep behind my colleague
items.description: In 10 years at the ABC, I've had some strange experiences. I can now add last week's CPAC conference in London to the list, and it's going somewhere near the top, says Riley Stuart in London.

items.title: How we got to Glasgow 2026 and what the Commonwealth Games will look like
items.description: The bumpy road to Glasgow 2026 has produced a Commonwealth Games that will look a little different than the ones that came before.

items.title: Why netball is growing into a sport of choice for men and boys
items.description: More young men are taking up netball at a competitive level. Competition organisers say there is less stigma around the sport among boys, with plenty of talent emerging.

items.title: AFL's first publicly gay player calls for respect in Crows-Pies match
items.description: Four months after becoming the first current or former AFL player to publicly come out as gay, Leigh Ryswyk is urging fans not to boo the Collingwood player targeted by Crow Izak Rankine’s homophobic slur.
